Fixed it to an exhaustive switch over all five `RecordingPersistedStatus` cases (`.recording`/`.interrupted`/`.finalizing` → stranded, `.finalized`/`.recoveredAfterUnexpectedExit` → leave alone) so a future new status forces a compile-time decision instead of silently falling through the way `.recording` just did.

Then, four iterations after I first said "blocked on `Entry`'s real initializer," it finally exists — so I wrote `Tests/RecordingReconcilerTests.swift` for real: in-memory `ModelContainer`, real on-disk `.caf` files written via `AVAudioFile` at the exact path `RecordingController` actually uses, no mocks. Five tests, including one that specifically pins the regression I just fixed (`.recording`-status entry gets recovered, not just `.interrupted`) and one verifying actual audio duration gets read back correctly from disk rather than just zeroed.
